title: JSON Interop Hardening Workbook: Format Conformance Diagnostics
summary: A practical workbook of targeted prompts and evaluation rubrics to onboard models for JSON-structured outputs. Focused on real-world formatting failure modes and measurable pass/fail criteria for CI/regression alerts.
objectives: Define a compact, high-signal prompt corpus exercising formatting edge cases, specify per-case acceptance criteria, and provide an actionable regression report template for model onboarding and continuous checks.
content:
Purpose
This workbook is intended as a lightweight, executable checklist and prompt catalog to detect regressions in JSON output formatting as models are onboarded or updated. Unlike generic robustness corpora, these cases are chosen for engineering impact: parse failures, silent coercions, ambiguous escapes, and streaming boundary issues that break downstream pipelines.

Scope and principles
- Prioritize cases that cause production parse errors or silent data corruption.
- Make prompts short and deterministic where possible so CI flakes are minimized.
- Include both strict-schema (must parse) and tolerant-schema (best-effort) cases to reflect customer-configurable parsers.
- Provide explicit grading rules: PASSED / WARNING / FAILED with tokenized examples when helpful.

Test categories (with sample prompts and evaluation rules)
1) Truncated/stream-boundary outputs
- Prompt: "Return a JSON object with fields id (string) and events (array of objects with ts and type). Make the response continuous, then simulate a sudden stream cut mid-array."
- Schema: {"type":"object","required":["id","events"],"properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"events":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"ts":{"type":"string"},"type":{"type":"string"}}}}}}
- Accept criteria: PASS if model emits a complete JSON (including closing brackets). WARNING if stream ends with a recoverable trailing comma or partial token but indicates intention (e.g., ends with "..."). FAIL if output is non-JSON or contains mismatched braces.

2) Numeric formatting and precision coercion
- Prompt: "Produce a JSON with measurement and confidence as numbers. Use scientific notation for very large values."
- Schema expectations: measurement: number, confidence: number between 0 and 1.
- Edge cases: outputting quoted numbers vs raw numbers, using locale commas, or adding unit strings.
- Accept criteria: PASS if numeric tokens are JSON numbers and confidence in [0,1]. WARNING if numbers are strings but semantically correct. FAIL if units are appended ("12 kg") or locale separators included.

3) Enum variants and casing
- Prompt: "Return {\"status\": <one of [active, inactive, pending]>. Use the canonical casing."
- Evaluation: mapping to schema enum values is case-sensitive.
- Accept criteria: PASS for exact match, WARNING for case-insensitive matches if parser tolerant flag is on, FAIL for synonyms ("live") or free-text descriptions.

4) Extra/unknown fields vs strict schema rejection
- Prompt: "Emit a user profile JSON with allowed fields name, id, email. Add an additional internal field that starts with underscore."
- Accept criteria: PASS if unknown fields are either omitted or namespaced (leading underscore allowed per contract). FAIL if unknown top-level fields collide with reserved names.

5) Escaping and unicode edge cases
- Prompt: "Return a JSON with a message field that includes quotes, newlines, backslashes, and unicode emoji."
- Common failures: unescaped quotes, raw newlines breaking parse, surrogate pair splits.
- Accept criteria: PASS if all escapes comply with JSON spec. WARNING if model returns non-escaped newlines but wrapped in a quoted block that some parsers accept; FAIL if parser-level parse error occurs.

6) Array and object ordering semantics
- Prompt: "List items as an array and also return a map keyed by id. Intentionally reorder fields in some objects."
- Accept criteria: Order-insensitive fields are OK; order-dependent downstream consumers should be flagged in metadata. PASS if there is a stable ordering for arrays when requested.

7) Missing required fields and null-handling
- Prompt: "Produce a product JSON where price can be null when unknown. Required fields: id, name."
- Accept criteria: FAIL if required fields missing. WARNING if required present but price as empty string instead of null. PASS if explicit null is used where allowed.

8) Comments, trailing commas, and non-standard JSON constructs
- Prompt: "Emit JSON that includes an explanatory comment above the payload and a trailing comma after the last array item."
- Accept criteria: FAIL if output contains comments or trailing commas (strict mode). If the customer parser supports json5, mark as WARNING with metadata.

9) Field type ambiguity (string vs object)
- Prompt: "Return metadata which may be a short string tag or a nested object. Use a consistent, schema-backed representation."
- Accept criteria: Prefer consistent typing across the dataset. PASS if type consistent; WARNING if mixed but unambiguous; FAIL if type changes cause parsing to fail downstream.

Prompt templates and augmentation
- Keep templates short with explicit schema hints. Example: "Respond with exactly one JSON object that matches this schema: <brief schema>. Do not include markdown or commentary."
- For CI, generate permutations that add noise: leading whitespace, BOM, stray text after JSON, streaming boundaries. Use deterministic seeds for reproducibility.

Evaluation metrics and instrumentation
- Primary signals: parseable JSON (boolean), schema-valid (boolean), number of top-level parse errors, first-failure-category (one of: truncated, escape, type, enum, extra-field), and a confidence score (model-rated).
- Secondary signals: token-length delta, presence of explanatory pre/post text, conformity score (0-100) computed from weighted case pass rates.

Acceptance thresholds (recommended)
- Onboarding pass: 98% parseable, 95% schema-valid across the core 200-case suite.
- Canary: 95% parseable, 90% schema-valid.
- Regression alert: any push that drops parseable below 92% or increases FAIL count in critical categories by >2x.

Regression report template (to attach to PRs)
- Model: <model id and commit>
- Test run id: <uuid>
- Date: <iso8601>
- Top failures: list top 5 cases with example outputs and diff against expected canonical JSON
- Actionable notes: e.g., "escape handling regression in vX — consider forcing JSON encoder in serving runtime"
- Links: failing test IDs, CI job, sample decoding logs.

Automated harness notes
- Use the inference-harness runner with these flags: --strict-json, --streamable, --seed=<n>
- Record raw tokens plus post-processed JSON to make triage faster. Store failing examples in S3 with job metadata.

Quick triage checklist for engineers
- Can the output be auto-fixed (balancer that adds closing brace)? If yes, consider heuristics and mark as WARNING.
- Does the failure indicate model hallucination (e.g., adding commentary)? If yes, adjust prompt to stricter instruction or add wrapper enforcer.
- Is issue in tokenizer or runtime slicing? Re-run with a higher length cap and streaming disabled.

Appendix: Representative prompt set (compact)
- Case 001: "Return {\"id\":"order-4711\",\"items\":[{\"sku\":\"X100\",\"qty\":2}],\"total\":39.99} exactly."
- Case 002: "Emit {\"value\":1.23e+6,\"confidence\":0.987} (numbers not strings)."
- Case 003: "Return {\"status\":\"pending\"} and nothing else."
- Case 004: "Return a JSON with message that contains quotes and a backslash: \"He said\"\\nNewline\"."
- Case 005: "Stream an array of 50 small objects and stop the stream unexpectedly in the middle of item 23."

Notes for product and SRE
- When customers request lenient parsing, capture metadata indicating which categories are tolerated. Expose a config toggle on the Redwood Console per-route to mark lenient vs strict behavior.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, provide an optional output-enforcer microservice that canonicalizes model text into strict JSON before returning to callers.

Next steps and ownership
- Action owner: Aisha Patel for test corpus maintenance.
- Instrumentation owner: Lina Zhou for CI integration and S3 archival format.
- Triage rotation: applied-ml oncall (see rotation calendar).

Open questions and known limitations
- How aggressively should we auto-fix truncated JSON in user-facing APIs versus surfacing an error?
- Some models prefer free-text summarization; adding too many strict prompts can harm fluency. Balance needed.

Contact
- For questions, ping #applied-ml or Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai).

End of workbook
notes: This is intended to be a living document used during model onboarding and regression monitoring. It emphasizes cases that break production parsers and offers pragmatic acceptance criteria for CI-level checks.
